concerns: Capture-enrichment may select non-EV particles (lipoproteins/aggregates) that resist mucin and bind the chosen reagent, confounding interpretation — experiment-level controls to exclude this are required (density/biochemical orthogonality, proteomics).

Simulated nasal-mucus and device-shear conditions may introduce assay interference (matrix effects) causing false negatives or false positives; while the proposal lists spike-in controls, formal pre-validation data are absent.

Driedonks et al. (macaque) report negligible intranasal brain uptake and strong nasal retention; this contradicts any implicit expectation that preserving surface epitopes alone will ensure large-species intranasal exposure — species, formulation, and administration-route explanations remain competing hypotheses and require short-interval in vivo bridging experiments in NHP or other large models before translational claims.

Manufacturability and yield risks: even if analytically discriminating, capture-enriched fractions may have insufficient yield/scalability; proposal notes this but lacks any preliminary yield estimates or orthogonal capture scalability evidence.

The proposal's inferential steps are correctly labeled as inferences, but the experiment-to-decision path depends critically on qualitative (yes/no) readouts; lack of predefined quantitative thresholds may complicate reproducibility and CMC gating.
conclusion: Supported with important evidence gaps. The proposal correctly cites MISEV2023 for methodological rigor and rodent studies (Hermann, Kodali) for intranasal preclinical functional signals while acknowledging non-human-primate limitations (Driedonks). The core inferences are appropriately labeled as inferences and not presented as validated in vivo clinical/large-animal proof. However, direct evidence that a mucin-resistant capture step (a) selectively enriches bona fide membrane-protected small EVs versus non-EV particles after mucin/device stress, and (b) yields in vivo-recoverable EV exposure in a large species, is missing — these are required to justify advancing the capture-enriched attribute toward manufacturing or translational decisions.
evidence_gap: No direct experimental evidence supports that a mucin-resistant capture-enriched fraction (as operationalized) selectively retains bona fide membrane-protected EVs (vs lipoproteins/aggregates) after simulated nasal-mucus and device passage, nor that such fractions yield short-interval in vivo recoverability/exposure in a large species (non-human primate) after intranasal administration. Also missing are documented assay-compatibility spike-in recovery results demonstrating that the proposed simulated-mucus/device conditions do not create false-positive protected signals or false-negative loss of genuine EV signal.
